name: Hypothesis Testing
description: ... then the theory behind estimators and tests: moments, sufficiency, information, likelihood ratios and chi-squared tests.

requires.why: Uses standard errors and the sampling distribution of the mean for z statistics and p-values.
Uses the chi-square, Gamma and t distributions and joint densities for information and test statistics.
The multinomial and Cauchy-Schwarz appear in two derivations; a quick check helps.

lessonObjectives.l1-could-be-luck: Frame a claim as a null and an alternative hypothesis.
lessonObjectives.l2-measuring-surprise: Compute a $z$ statistic for a sample mean.
lessonObjectives.l3-p-value: Compute a p-value and say exactly what it is a probability of.
lessonObjectives.l4-t-test: Use a $t$ test for a mean and compare it with the $z$ test.
lessonObjectives.l5-two-ways-wrong: Tell type I from type II errors, and trade one against the other.
lessonObjectives.l6-power: Compute the power of a test and choose a sample size.
lessonObjectives.l7-what-p-is-not: Spot the common misreadings of a p-value.
lessonObjectives.l8-two-groups: Test a difference between two means.
lessonObjectives.l9-twenty-tests: See how running many tests produces false discoveries.
lessonObjectives.l10-correcting: Apply the Bonferroni correction and control the false discovery rate.
lessonObjectives.l11-is-sharpe-real: Test a strategy’s Sharpe ratio and adjust for the number of strategies tried.
lessonObjectives.l12-data-snooping: Recognise data snooping, and see why factor research now asks for a $t$ statistic above 3.
lessonObjectives.l13-matching-moments: Estimate parameters by the method of moments and compare the result with maximum likelihood.
lessonObjectives.l14-what-data-can-forget: Recognise a sufficient statistic with the factorisation theorem, and improve an estimator by conditioning on it.
lessonObjectives.l15-sharpness-of-the-peak: Compute the Fisher information of a model and use it for the standard error of a maximum likelihood estimate.
lessonObjectives.l16-best-possible-precision: Derive the Cramér-Rao bound and decide whether an unbiased estimator attains it.
lessonObjectives.l17-ratio-of-likelihoods: Build the most powerful test of two simple hypotheses, and use the chi-squared limit for a likelihood-ratio test.
lessonObjectives.l18-counts-against-expectations: Run chi-squared tests of goodness of fit and of independence, with the right degrees of freedom.
